paragraphs: Asiyyat ohel qeba hi toledet boneh vaasura beshabbat min hattora, velaken ameru rabbotenu za"l: asur laasot ohel bashshabbat o beyom tob, dehaynu gag hammaahil alayv lehagen min hachamma o miggeshamim o meezeh dabar acher; vaapillu hu ohel aray sheeno asuy lehitqayyem, ella raq hu lepi shaa; vaapillu sheen mechitztzot tachtayv, kegon shepparas machtzelet "g arba qundasin, ap al pi ken, kevan deasuy kede lehaahil ulehagen, hare zeh ohel gamur, vaasaruhu chakamim "p shehu aray, gezera mishshum ohel qeba shehu toledet boneh veasur min hattora. velo aseru ella laasoto battechilla beshabbat, abal im haya ohel aray asuy mibbeod yom, muttar lehosip alayv beshabbat - kegon im hayeta machtzelet perusa mibbeod yom kede tepach shehu shiur ohel, muttar leparsa kullah lemachar ulehosip od machtzelaot, shekkol zeh hu tosepet leohel tepach heasuy meetmol; vaapillu lipros al mechitztzot muttar beinyan zeh. vetepach sheameru, hu chutz min hakkerika shel hammachtzelet, d"p shezzo hammachtzelet shehiyyatah netuna mibbeod yom hayeta keruka beiggul sheyyesh beheqqepah shelosha tepachim, deaz yesh bah rochab tepach bevadday, im kol zeh la mehanne zeh, ella tzarik sheyyehe yotze mimmenna kede tepach parus leohel, mippene dehakkerika atzmah enah niret keohel; umihu, lechumera chayeshinan lah, dehaynu im hammachtzelet keruka, veyesh beobi iggul kerikatah kede tepach, asur lehannichah beshabbat al gab dabar shettihyeh keohel, v"g deamarnu disbib haiggul eno nireh keohel, mikkol maqom lechumera chashib ohel, ukemo shekkatab ha"ture-zahab" za"l.

clarification.explanation: Making a permanent tent (a roof that protects from sun, rain, and the like) is a derivative of the forbidden labor of "building," and is Torah-forbidden on the Sabbath. Even a temporary tent, meant to last only a short while, and even without walls beneath it (such as a mat spread over four posts), is forbidden, since the Sages made a decree against a temporary tent out of concern it might lead to a permanent one. But this applies only to making it as the primary practice; if a temporary tent was already made before the Sabbath (such as a mat already spread to the measure of a handbreadth), it is permitted to add to it on the Sabbath, even spreading it over supports. The measure of a "handbreadth" refers to material actually spread out, not rolled up. The prohibition against making a tent applies equally on the Sabbath and on a festival.
takeaways: It is forbidden to make a tent (even temporary) on the Sabbath as the primary practice — a rabbinic decree around a Torah prohibition
If a handbreadth was already spread out before the Sabbath, it is permitted to add to it on the Sabbath

paragraphs: Ha deaseru chaza"l gam baaray, hu davqa beohel shehu gag, abal mechitztza shel aray muttar laasot lekattechilla beshabbat, vaapillu sheoseh otah kede lehagen min hachamma o min hatztzinna, la chashiba keohel bishbil kak; veken im oseh otah bishbil hannerot shello yekabbu, o sheoseh otah litzniut bealema, kegon lehapsiq ben anashim lenashim shello yiru zeh et zeh, veken kayyotze bazeh, shari; mihu, im oseh otah lehattir sukka o lehattir shear issur, ukegon sheoseh mechitztza asara tepachim mippene hasseparim biprisat sadin o machtzelet kede sheyyehe muttar leshammesh mittato o laasot tzerakayv vekayyotze bazeh, apillu shehi mechitztzat aray, asur; kevan sheasuya lehattir ezeh dabar haasur. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti, dehu haddin im pores sadin keneged maqom sheyyesh bo tzoa - im hu beinyan deim lo haya pores hassadin haya asur liqrot, dachashib lah asuya lehattir dabar haasur, veasur lipros hassadin; veraq im haya beinyan dahava epshar likpot al hattinnup keli veliqrot, shari lipros sadin, kevan deepshar lehattir haasur beopen acher; veayyen "tosepet-shabbat", seip qatan v, mah shekkatab hetter zeh mah"ture zahab" za"l; yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: The prohibition on a temporary tent applies specifically to a "roof" (the covering element), but it is permitted to make a temporary standing partition on the Sabbath as the primary practice — even to protect from heat or cold, to prevent candles from being extinguished, or for modesty (to separate men from women). But if the partition was made in order to permit another prohibition (such as a ten-handbreadth partition to permit marital relations, or to cover excrement without which the Shema cannot be recited) — it is forbidden, even though temporary, since it is "made to permit a prohibition"; unless it is possible to cover the filth with a vessel instead of a sheet.
takeaways: A partition (unlike a roof) is permitted even temporarily — for heat, cold, candles, or modesty
A partition meant "to permit a prohibition" is forbidden even if temporary

paragraphs: Vilon hattaluy lipne happetach bimqom delet, "p shehu taluy sham biqbiut, muttar litloto beshabbat, dekevan shehu na vanad berucha metzuya, vegam eno meakkeb laoberim veshabim derek sham, eno niqra mechitztza qebua ella mechitztzat aray, vekol dela asuya lehattir, shari. veken hu haddin yesh lehattir mittaam zeh litlot happaroket lipne aron haqqodesh apillu en sham delet, ella happaroket atzmah hi mechitztza laaron. vetzarik lizzaher keshettoleh havvilon vekayyotze, shello yitqappel veyikpol lerachebbo tepach beshaa shettoleh oto, denimtza oseh ohel baggag tepach; lepikak, im hu vilon gadol, tolin oto shenayim, kede sheyyitluhu kullo keechad velo yitqappel, abal adam echad, asur.

clarification.explanation: A curtain hung in front of a doorway (in place of a door) may be hung on the Sabbath, since it moves in the wind and does not block passersby — it is not considered a permanent partition. Likewise it is permitted to hang a curtain in front of the Holy Ark for this reason. But one must be careful that the curtain not fold over to a width of a handbreadth while being hung (which would make it a "roof" of a handbreadth) — therefore a large curtain should be hung by two people together, not by one person alone.
takeaways: A curtain hung in a doorway is permitted on the Sabbath (it is not a permanent partition)
One must be careful it does not fold to a handbreadth's width while being hung — a large curtain should be hung by two people

paragraphs: Etzim hassedurim meereb shabbat veyesh berachebbam tepach, hare zeh muttar lipros alehem sadin o machtzelet beshabbat kede lesheb tachtam, dehave tosepet ohel vekaamur leel; vehu haddin im en berochab haetzim tepach, ella shehem semukim zeh lazeh, sheen ben achat leachat shelosha tepachim dehave labud - muttar lipros alehem sadin; v"p deetzim ellu qebuim kol hayyamim, uporesin alehem sadin keshetztzerikim lekak, mikkol maqom kevan deyesh baetzim rochab tepach, chashib tosepet ohel.

Veken hu haddin laarubba shebbaggag sheppetucha betok haqqaruy, muttar lipros aleha sadin beshabbat bishbil hashshemesh o harucha, deen zeh ella tosepet ohel; mihu, im yesh laarubba zo peqaq sheeno asuy lehippateach tadir ella raq leittim rechoqim, asur lipqoq beshabbat "p sheppaqaq zeh muttar betiltul, mishshum kevan deeno asuy lehippateach ella leittim rechoqim, machze kemosip al habbinyan - hen baarubba shebbaggag, hen bachallon shebbakkotel - ukemo shekkatab "magen-abraham", siman shyg, seip qatan , ubeshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman za"l, seip '; veayyen "eshel-abraham" sham. vehinneh poh irenu yesh bebatte-kenesiyyot ammudim mesuddarim veomedim bammaarab ubammizrach veken batztzapon vedarom shealehem omedet hattiqra, vehechatzer battavek; ak betok hechatzer yesh gam ken ammudim bearba zaviyyot vaalehem omedet tiqra, vetachat tiqra hazzot munnachat hatteba shel bet-hakkeneset beemtza, usebib zo hattiqra asher hatteba tachteha yesh avir chatzer mearba ruchoteha; uminhagam beyom-kippur lipros machtzelaot al avir hechatzer missabib mippene hashshemesh hannikneset bebet-hakkeneset al hayyoshebim sham. v"p sheellu haetzim hammetuchim baavir hechatzer hahi uqebuim sham tamid en bahem tepach, en kan chashash mishshum ohel, deen anachnu tzerikin letappeach al haetzim hahem, yaan ki sham yesh zizin boletin al avir hechatzer hannizkar missabib bekol hatztzedadin, veal yede ken nechshabin hammachtzelaot shepporesin otam beyom-kippur tosepet ohel. gam od belav haki - mishshum hattiqra atzmah gam ken nechshab perisat hammachtzelet letosepet ohel, vahare zeh domeh ledin arubba shebbaggag hannizkar leel. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" nistappaqti: heka deyesh etzim metuchim baavir mikkotel zeh lekotel zeh, veyesh bahem rochab tepach, ak haetzim husemu sham bishbil shello yitnodedu hakketalim - im chashib perisat hassadin alehem letosepet ohel veshari; velo nipshat etzli sapeq zeh.

clarification.explanation:
Beams arranged before the Sabbath, a handbreadth wide, may have a sheet or mat spread over them on the Sabbath to sit beneath them, since this is considered "adding to an existing tent" (an addition to an existing tent, not building a new one). The same law applies if the beams are less than a handbreadth wide but are close together, within three handbreadths of each other (considered "lavud," that is, connected) — a sheet may be spread over them. Even though the beams are fixed in place at all times and the sheet is spread only when needed, since the beams have the width of a handbreadth, this is considered an addition to a tent and not a new tent. Likewise, a chimney opening in the roof into the house may have a sheet spread over it on the Sabbath against the sun or wind, for the same reason. But if the chimney has a stopper (a cover) that is opened only rarely, it is forbidden to close it on the Sabbath (even though it is permitted to handle it), since this appears as an addition to the building, both for a roof chimney and for a wall window.
The Ben Ish Chai adds an example from the reality of his city: in the synagogues of Baghdad there are pillars arranged to the east, west, north, and south, on which the ceiling stands, with a courtyard in the middle. Within that courtyard there are additional pillars at the four corners on which a separate ceiling stands, beneath which stands the synagogue's reading platform, with open courtyard air on all four sides around this ceiling. It is customary on Yom Kippur to spread mats around this courtyard air, to protect those sitting from the sun entering the synagogue. Even though the beams stretched there in the courtyard air are not a handbreadth wide, there is no concern of the prohibition of a tent — since there are protruding ledges along the courtyard air on all sides, and also because of the ceiling itself, so that spreading the mats is considered merely "an addition to a tent," similar to the law of the roof chimney. He notes that an unresolved doubt remains for him: a case of beams stretched in the air from wall to wall, a handbreadth wide, but placed there only to prevent the walls from swaying (not for the purpose of spreading a sheet) — whether spreading a sheet over them is also considered "an addition to a tent" and permitted, or not.
takeaways: Beams arranged before the Sabbath a handbreadth wide (or close together within three handbreadths) may have a sheet spread over them on the Sabbath — this is a permitted "addition to a tent"
A roof chimney may be covered with a sheet on the Sabbath against sun or wind, but a stopper opened only rarely may not be closed on the Sabbath

In synagogues with an open courtyard (such as the Yom Kippur custom in Baghdad), mats may be spread over the courtyard air against the sun, when protruding ledges or a ceiling make this "an addition to a tent"
An unresolved doubt remains: beams stretched between walls only to prevent swaying (not for spreading) — whether a sheet may be spread over them

paragraphs: Kol ohel deasur laasoto beshabbat, hu haddin name deasur lesatero velahasiro beshabbat, ki keshem deasur libnot ken asur listor habbinyan.

clarification.explanation: Any tent forbidden to make on the Sabbath is also forbidden to dismantle and remove on the Sabbath, just as it is forbidden to build, so it is forbidden to dismantle.
takeaways: The prohibition on making a tent applies equally to dismantling or removing it

paragraphs: Ha degazeru ohel aray "g deen tachtayv mechitztzot, davqa betzarik laavir shettachtayv, abal im eno mitkavven kede sheyyaahil al mah shettachtayv, shari. laken: mitta veshulchan, deen hammechitztzot mechubbarim biqrashim, sheddarkan lesadder haqqerashim al hammechitztzot, muttar lesadderam beshabbat "g dehaqqerashim maahilim al avir shettachtam, kevan sheeno tzarik lazeh, ki ellu en asuyin lashebet tachtam o lehannicha dabar tachtam, ella raq mishtammeshin alehem lemala.

Bammeh debarim amurim? heka dimchitztzot shellahem enam maggiim ad haaretz, abal im maggiim ad haaretz kemo dipne hatteba, o shehem semukim laaretz bepachot mishshelosha tepachim dehave labud, hare zeh asur lesadder halluchot shehem qarqa hammitta vehashshulchan alehem, v"p sheeno tzarik laavir shettachtam kelal, demeachar deikka mechitztzot gemurot ad haaretz, nireh tepe keohel veasur; mihu, yesh machmirin veoserin bammitta gam heka deen mechitztzot gemurot ella omedet al arba qundasin, mishshum demishtammesh baavir shettachteha shemmannicha sham chapatzim, v"g deen kavvanato baabur zeh velo lekak asuya, apillu hake machze keohel veasur, vetzarik lachush ledibrehem, daanachenu roin haolam mannichim chapatzim tachat hammittot, abal beshulchan en lachush bikhay gavna, deen lo mechitztzot gemurot, deen darkam shel bene-adam lehishtammesh baavir shettachat hashshulchan kelal; v"g deim yesh mesibba gedola mannichim baavir shettachat hashshulchan lipamim kelim meleim o reqanim lepi shaa - kevan deen osin ken ella raq bimsibba gedola, vegam bimsibba gedola lav kullehu enashe regili bekak, en lachush.

clarification.explanation: The decree on a temporary tent applies only when one needs the space beneath it; but if one does not intend to provide shelter for what is beneath it, it is permitted. Therefore a bed and a table, whose boards are not permanently attached to partitions, may be arranged on the Sabbath, since the intention is not to sit or place anything beneath them, but to use their surface. But if the partitions reach the ground (such as the sides of a chest), it is forbidden, since this appears more like a tent. Some are stringent even regarding a bed standing only on legs (even without complete partitions), since it is customary to place objects beneath it, and one should therefore be concerned for their opinion. But regarding a table there is no concern at all, since it is not people's way to use the space beneath a table; and even though at a large feast people sometimes place full or empty vessels briefly beneath the table, there is no concern in this, since it is not a fixed practice and not all those present at such a gathering are accustomed to it.
takeaways: A bed or table without partitions reaching the ground may be arranged on the Sabbath (there is no intent to provide shelter)
Partitions reaching the ground, or the habit of placing objects underneath (as with a bed), should be treated stringently
For a table, unlike a bed, there is no concern at all — even the occasional placing of vessels beneath it at a large feast is not a fixed practice and creates no concern

paragraphs: Kisa heasuy peraqim, ukesherotzim lesheb alayv potechim oto vehaor niptach venimtach, ukeshemmesirim oto, sogerin oto vehaor nikpal, muttar lepatecho lekattechilla beshabbat "p sheyyesh lo mechitztzot tachtayv, mippene sheeno domeh laasiyyat ohel, kevan sheeno oseh kelum, shehare hem asuyin veomedim kebar haggag im hammechitztzot mibbeod yom, ella shemmotechan beshabbat lesheb alehen.

clarification.explanation: A folding chair (with leather that opens and stretches when sat upon) may be opened on the Sabbath even though it has partitions beneath it, since one is not building anything new — the roof and partitions were already made before the Sabbath, and he is only stretching them in order to sit.
takeaways: A folding chair prepared in advance may be opened on the Sabbath, since this is not new construction

paragraphs: Keli sheqqorin bearbe "shemmasyi" (shimsheh) ubaitalqi "ymbrylh" (mitriyya) sheasuyim lehagen min hachamma umin haggeshamim - la mibbaaya deasur lepatechah lehaahil bah, ella apillu petucha veomedet mibbeod yom asur laset otah lehaahil bah al rosho, ben beshabbat, ben beyom tob vekannizkar bapposeqim. veayyen "maamar-mareddekay", seip Adonai v"noda bihuda" tinyana, siman l, yeuyyan sham. umimmela teda: meachar deasur lenasheah al rosho, asur name letaltelah beshabbat veyom tob mishshum muqtzeh.

clarification.explanation: A parasol or umbrella that protects from sun or rain may not be opened on the Sabbath to provide shelter, and even if it is already open from before the Sabbath, it is forbidden to carry it overhead on the Sabbath or a festival. Consequently, since it is forbidden to carry it, it is also forbidden to handle it on the Sabbath and festival under the law of muktzeh.
takeaways: A parasol or umbrella is forbidden both to open and to carry (even if already open beforehand), and even to handle, under the law of muktzeh

paragraphs: Asur lipros sadin al haetz hammunnach al haarisa shel tinoq sheqqorin bearbe "mehed" o "gelalah" (arisa mitnadnedet), ella im ken haya parus tepach meereb shabbat. vetzarik lehazhir hamon haam bazeh, ki poh irenu darkan lipros sadin al arisa hannizkar shel tinoq lehagen alayv mippene hachamma umin hazzebubin vekayyotze.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to spread a sheet over the wood above an infant's cradle (to protect from sun and flies), unless a handbreadth was already spread before the Sabbath — and the public should be cautioned about this, since it is common to do so.
takeaways: Spreading a protective sheet over an infant's cradle is permitted only if a handbreadth was already prepared before the Sabbath

paragraphs: Teba sheyyesh aleha kissuy, im eno qabua betzirim asur lehannicho aleha beshabbat o lahasiro mimmenna, "g deenah asuya ella lepetach bealema. veyesh omerim dekol zeh hu beteba shehi rechaba, veken bekelim kayyotze bah shehem rechabim dekissuyim domeh leohel, abal kelim qetannim, "p sheyyesh bahem chalal rachab tepach, en kissuyim domeh leohel veshari. veyesh choleqin leesor gam bekelim qetannim sheyyesh bahem chalal reqan tepach; mihu, lo aseru bazeh ella beheka deen hakkissuy meyuchad lahem, abal kissuy hamyuchad lahem, kevan sheddarko bekak tamid la machze keebed uhla kevan deen osin hammechitztzot beshabbat, ella omedin mealehem miqqamme shabbeta; umikkol maqom, im hu mekasseh otam bebeged, "g dimyuchad lahem, asur, mishshum ki bebeged en bo tiqqun hammokicha alayv shehu omed lekak; velaken kelim sheddarkam lehannicha bahem mirqachat o debash vekayyotze, sheddarkam listom pihem bachatikat beged mippene shello yikkanesu bahem nemalim vekayyotze tzerikin lehizzaher laasot lahem kissuy mecheres o etz, veyannichu chatikat habbeged lemala meoto kissuy, velo yekassu bahem bachatikat habbeged bilbad.

clarification.explanation: A box with a lid not fixed on hinges — it is forbidden to place it on the box or remove it on the Sabbath, even though it is meant only as a simple opening. Some say this applies only to a wide box (and similarly wide vessels), where such a lid resembles a "tent"; but small vessels, even if they have a cavity a handbreadth wide, their lid does not resemble a tent, and is permitted. Some disagree and forbid this also for small vessels with a handbreadth cavity; but they forbade it only when the lid is not specially designated for them — a lid specially designated for them, since this is always its way, does not appear as making a tent (since the walls have stood since before the Sabbath). Nevertheless, if one covers them with a garment — even if specially designated — it is forbidden, since a garment has no fixture proving it is meant for this. Therefore, vessels normally sealed at their mouth with a piece of cloth (so ants do not enter) should have a cover made of pottery or wood, with the cloth placed over that cover, rather than covering with the cloth alone.
takeaways: A lid not fixed on hinges may not be placed or removed on the Sabbath for a wide box (which resembles a tent)

For small vessels there is a dispute; a lid specially designated for them is permitted (since it does not appear as making a tent), but covering with a garment alone is forbidden — one should use a pottery or wood cover with the garment over it

paragraphs: Chabit sheyyesh bah mayim veenah melea kullah, ella yesh bah chalal shiur tepach reqan min hammayim - asur lishtoach aleha beged beshabbat lekassotah; vehu haddin im haya shatucha aleha beged asur lahasiro dahava lah soter ohel; abal im enah chasera tepach, sheen bah chalal avir reqan shiur tepach, en kan din ohel veshari. ketzad yaaseh bechabit shel mayim shehu mukrach lekassotah beshabbat? yabi meereb shabbat beged, vikasseh bah hechabit yoter mittepach, veyiqsherenna heteb kede shezzeh hakkissuy shel tepach lo yishshamet meal hechabit, veaz beyom-shabbat yukal lekassot hechabit bekissuy acher lemala meoto kissuy shel tepach sheasa mibbeod yom, o yekassenna bisherit habbeged hahu shel mekasseh hattepach. veda, ki bechabit shel mayim tzarik lemechash tepe: chada, shehi rechaba beyoter; veod, ki hammashqeh en rauy litten bikli beli kissuy, vehave keoseh mechitztzot gam ken. veayyen "ture-zahab" veshulchan aruk lerabbenu zalman v"chesed laalapim" ushear acharonim.

clarification.explanation: A water barrel not completely full (having an airspace of a handbreadth) — it is forbidden to spread a garment over it to cover it on the Sabbath, and likewise forbidden to remove a garment already covering it (dismantling a tent). If it has no handbreadth of airspace, it is permitted. The solution: prepare before the Sabbath a garment cover more than a handbreadth, tied securely, and then on the Sabbath an additional cover may be placed over it.
takeaways: A barrel with a handbreadth of airspace should not have its cover placed or removed on the Sabbath; the solution is to prepare a permanent cover before the Sabbath

paragraphs: Nohagin haolam likpot sal gadol al okalim lishmor otam, veen chosheshin mishshum ohel, dehassal yesh bo gag umechitztzot vehu tzarik laavir shettachtam. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti beinyan zeh, vesham hebeti dibre haggaon "eshel-abraham", siman sht"v, sop seip qatan ch', shekkatab beteba hammachazeqet arbaim sea, tzarik iyyun im muttar likpot al okalin umashqin veku', yeuyyan sham; upilpalti qetzat bidbarayv. veod hebeti sham mah shekkatab beshulchan aruk, siman shch, seip l"d, gabbe tinnup, dekopeh alayv keli, veken mah shekkatab beshulchan aruk, siman tm"v, seip ' useip g', gabbe chametz beshabbat veyom tob dekopeh alayv keli; vedochaq leparesh deayre beheka deen bikpiyya zo chalal reqan shiur tepach; veachar hachaluqim usebarot sheasiti bedabar zeh lo matzati reaya berura leminhag zeh; ak beemet hamminhag hazzeh poh irenu hu barur - hen bikpiyyat hassal al okalin umashqim hen bahasarat hassal mealehem legamre shezzoqepin oto al gabbayv; vekatabti lismok al chilluq echad shekkatabti sham leqayyem hamminhag. veayyen beshulchan aruk lerabbenu zalman za"l, besiman sh"v, seip k', v"erek-hashshulchan", siman sh"v, seip b'. umihu, im hassal gadol shemmachaziq arbaim sea, yesh lehachmir; vehannizhar gam beqatan tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: It is customary to place an overturned large basket over food for safekeeping, and there is no concern of the tent prohibition in this (even though the basket has a roof and walls and needs the space beneath it) — the local custom is supported despite the halachic doubt, both in placing the basket and in removing it. For very large baskets (holding forty se'ah), one should be stringent.
takeaways: Overturning a basket over food for safekeeping is an accepted custom despite the doubt; for a very large basket, one should be stringent
